note: The authored layout of the raft town in the Sound. A template has no position; this file is the placement data. tools/sea_town.py translates it into the settlement record, the Centre and Mart placements and one earthwork per district in data/placements.json (so tools/place_town.py builds it as a town, re-apply step R8), refuses a raft over land or over water shallower than its rule, overlapping elements, a bridge that does not join two decks, and a deck walk cell below min_light in its lantern model. Ground is the canonical heightmap (tools/ground.py, rounded), never a world: the seabed under a post is round(h) and the deck is the world's sea level from data/world.json. Coordinates are inclusive [x0, z0, x1, z1] rectangles.

site.why_here: the bank's crown, shaped for the town by data/water_shape.json jungle_isle_bank (measured on the copy by python tools/sea_town.py plan --resite --heightmap derived/water_shape/land_8k_16_rescaled_b145_pads_rift_water.png): 3-6 deep under the rafts, sand shallows 1-2 deep round the Stilt Quarter and the yard, the blue hole off Fishers' Row's head, and 8-14 deep bank water beyond, so the town's only rest ground is the town

levels.deck: data/world.json vertical.sea_level (y62): the deck replaces the top water layer

rules.why: Rafts, piers and the gate's raft float over at least 3 blocks of water, so a boat passes round them and the posts are visible; the walks that come ashore (the jetty, the yard's wharf, the stilt boardwalk) may reach the beach, never ground above the deck. Lanterns (never light blocks): one on a post at every raft corner and every lamp_every blocks along the edges and walks, and the tool refuses the plan if its model leaves any open deck cell at the walk level below min_light.

Boats are vanilla, not Cobblemon items, and the town is otherwise reachable only by swimming or a water mount.

settlement_text.reading: Out on the open sea south of the plateau, where the Jungle Isle once stood, a town floats over the drowned island's bank: sixteen log rafts on posts to the sand, joined by bamboo bridges, a hut on each. The Centre and the Mart stand on the two largest, either side of the square with its waystone. Fishers' Row runs 120 blocks west to the lip of the bank's blue hole, a station every eight blocks, the Fishing Guild at its root. North-east over the sand shallows is the boatwright's wharf with a hull in frame; south, the Stilt Quarter's houses and the inn stand in the shallows on mangrove stilts. There is no road and no shore: the ferry puts out from a jetty on the plateau's beach 700 blocks north, and to the south-west a floating boom and a lookout watch the bank's open water.
